title: your light is also your health and your score — stuck on making the crypts actually escalate
author: desperate-effort-1
selftext:
made a little dungeon crawler called Wick with AI over the last few weeks and i've hit a design wall i can't think my way out of, so asking people who've actually built this kind of thing.

the setup: you're a candle-headed knight descending crypts. your flame is your light radius, your timer and your score, all the same number. it burns down constantly, wax on the floor tops it up. everything outside the radius is pitch black. so the thing keeping you alive is also the only thing letting you see, and spending it to explore is the whole tension.

that part works, i like it. the problem is crypt 1 and crypt 5 feel the same.

everything i have reached for to escalate has been a number. burn faster. more wraiths. bigger levels. all of it makes runs shorter or more irritating without making them more interesting, and bigger levels are actively worse — more time walking through black with nothing happening.

what i think i want is for the DARK to get more interesting rather than the enemy count going up. things i have considered but not built: rooms that stay lit after you leave, so routing matters. something that eats your radius on contact, so the light itself is under threat instead of just draining. a crypt where wax is everywhere but the layout is a maze, so light becomes time pressure rather than health. no idea which of those is the good one, or if it's none of them.

so the actual question: if you've built a game where one resource does several jobs at once, what made your later levels genuinely different rather than just tighter? i keep landing on "same thing but meaner" and that's obviously not the answer.

second thing, art. all of it is generated. the candle reads fine and the light gradient carries a lot, but the environment is the weak part — the tiles are flat and it feels like a grid rather than a place. if you've made something this dark, how did you get texture and depth into stuff the player can barely see, without lighting it and killing the point of the game?

on the AI side, mechanics were the easy part. "your light is your health" got a working prototype almost immediately. the time went into tuning — burn rate vs wax density vs radius size all fight each other, and no model has any idea what feels good. that's still just playing your own game and moving one number at a time.

link if you want to try it. the single most useful thing anyone could tell me is "i stopped caring at crypt 2":

https://preview.redd.it/rp53csm9ynlh1.jpg?width=1536&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=2b73f9230a99257fa83a4a570f16326056bce7f0
